newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian shares end firm, market seen tethered.
newsitem.headline: Austrian shares end firm, market seen tethered.

text.p: Austrian shares resisted weak international leads to end moderately firm on Friday, but traders held out little hope for significant moves next week.

"There should be more bias on the upside than the downside next week. I see 1,040 points as the lower limit," said one trader, who traced today's recovery from a low of 1,031.98 to "basically not so bad sentiment in the market."
The ATX index of 21 blue chips ended 1.45 points, or 0.14 percent, higher at 1,039.93, with nine shares higher, 11 lower, and one unchanged.
Another trader said he expects the ATX to be stuck within its tight range of 1,020 to 1,050 points next week.

The day's best performer was luxury hosiery manufacturer Wolford, up 3.75 percent at 2,490 schillings, while the worst was Creditanstalt's preferred shares, down 1.40 percent to a new year low of 470.3.
Savings bank Die Erste said it would not be able to submit its final bid for acquiring the state's stake in Creditanstalt by the end of today -- the deadline set by Finance Minister Viktor Klima.
The broad-based Vienna Bourse index added on 0.15 percent to close at 405.77.
The September ATX future lost 2.6 points to 1,037.9 on turnover of 303 contracts.
